GO PROGRAMMING GUIDE

This document explains core concepts of the Go programming language.

Overview (section 1)
====================

Go is a statically typed, compiled language designed at Google for simplicity, concurrency, and fast builds. It emphasizes explicit error handling and a small language spec.

Variables and Types (section 1)
===============================

Declare variables with var or := for inference. Basic types include int, float64, string, bool, arrays, slices, maps, and structs. Zero values apply when variables are uninitialized.

Control Flow (section 1)
========================

if, for, and switch handle control flow. Go has no while keyword; for loops cover iteration. defer schedules cleanup calls when a function returns.

Functions (section 1)
=====================

Functions are declared with func name(args) returnType. Multiple return values are idiomatic, especially (value, error). Functions are first-class but not fully generic until Go 1.18+ generics.

Structs and Methods (section 1)
===============================

Structs group fields. Methods attach to types via receiver functions: func (s *T) Method(). Pointer receivers allow mutation and avoid copying large values.

Interfaces (section 1)
======================

Interfaces define behavior by method sets. A type satisfies an interface implicitly. Small interfaces such as io.Reader encourage composable designs.

Concurrency (section 1)
=======================

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Error Handling (section 1)
==========================

Functions return error as the last value. if err != nil is the standard pattern. errors.Is and errors.As unwrap wrapped errors. panic/recover handle exceptional cases sparingly.

Modules (section 1)
===================

go mod init creates a module. go get fetches dependencies. go build, go test, and go run are core commands. The go toolchain vendors reproducible builds.

Testing (section 1)
===================

Testing uses the testing package in *_test.go files. Table-driven tests are common. go test ./... runs packages. Benchmarks and examples integrate with the toolchain.

Standard Library (section 1)
============================

net/http serves HTTP APIs. encoding/json handles JSON. database/sql connects to SQL databases. The standard library favors batteries-included production utilities.

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

===========================

if, for, and switch handle control flow. Go has no while keyword; for loops cover iteration. defer schedules cleanup calls when a function returns.

Functions (section 32)
======================

Functions are declared with func name(args) returnType. Multiple return values are idiomatic, especially (value, error). Functions are first-class but not fully generic until Go 1.18+ generics.

Structs and Methods (section 32)
================================

Structs group fields. Methods attach to types via receiver functions: func (s *T) Method(). Pointer receivers allow mutation and avoid copying large values.

Interfaces (section 32)
=======================

Interfaces define behavior by method sets. A type satisfies an interface implicitly. Small interfaces such as io.Reader encourage composable designs.

Concurrency (section 32)
========================

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Error Handling (section 32)
===========================

Functions return error as the last value. if err != nil is the standard pattern. errors.Is and errors.As unwrap wrapped errors. panic/recover handle exceptional cases sparingly.

Modules (section 32)
====================

go mod init creates a module. go get fetches dependencies. go build, go test, and go run are core commands. The go toolchain vendors reproducible builds.

Testing (section 32)
====================

Testing uses the testing package in *_test.go files. Table-driven tests are common. go test ./... runs packages. Benchmarks and examples integrate with the toolchain.

Standard Library (section 32)
=============================

net/http serves HTTP APIs. encoding/json handles JSON. database/sql connects to SQL databases. The standard library favors batteries-included production utilities.

Overview (section 48)
=====================

Go is a statically typed, compiled language designed at Google for simplicity, concurrency, and fast builds. It emphasizes explicit error handling and a small language spec.

Variables and Types (section 48)
================================

Declare variables with var or := for inference. Basic types include int, float64, string, bool, arrays, slices, maps, and structs. Zero values apply when variables are uninitialized.

Control Flow (section 48)
=========================

if, for, and switch handle control flow. Go has no while keyword; for loops cover iteration. defer schedules cleanup calls when a function returns.

Functions (section 48)
======================

Functions are declared with func name(args) returnType. Multiple return values are idiomatic, especially (value, error). Functions are first-class but not fully generic until Go 1.18+ generics.

Structs and Methods (section 48)
================================

Structs group fields. Methods attach to types via receiver functions: func (s *T) Method(). Pointer receivers allow mutation and avoid copying large values.

Interfaces (section 48)
=======================

Interfaces define behavior by method sets. A type satisfies an interface implicitly. Small interfaces such as io.Reader encourage composable designs.

Concurrency (section 48)
========================

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Error Handling (section 48)
===========================

Functions return error as the last value. if err != nil is the standard pattern. errors.Is and errors.As unwrap wrapped errors. panic/recover handle exceptional cases sparingly.

Modules (section 48)
====================

go mod init creates a module. go get fetches dependencies. go build, go test, and go run are core commands. The go toolchain vendors reproducible builds.

Interfaces define behavior by method sets. A type satisfies an interface implicitly. Small interfaces such as io.Reader encourage composable designs.

Concurrency (section 63)
========================

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Error Handling (section 63)
===========================

Functions return error as the last value. if err != nil is the standard pattern. errors.Is and errors.As unwrap wrapped errors. panic/recover handle exceptional cases sparingly.

====================

Declare variables with var or := for inference. Basic types include int, float64, string, bool, arrays, slices, maps, and structs. Zero values apply when variables are uninitialized.

Control Flow (section 79)
=========================

if, for, and switch handle control flow. Go has no while keyword; for loops cover iteration. defer schedules cleanup calls when a function returns.

Functions (section 79)
======================

Functions are declared with func name(args) returnType. Multiple return values are idiomatic, especially (value, error). Functions are first-class but not fully generic until Go 1.18+ generics.

Structs and Methods (section 79)
================================

Structs group fields. Methods attach to types via receiver functions: func (s *T) Method(). Pointer receivers allow mutation and avoid copying large values.

Interfaces (section 79)
=======================

Interfaces define behavior by method sets. A type satisfies an interface implicitly. Small interfaces such as io.Reader encourage composable designs.

Concurrency (section 79)
========================

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Error Handling (section 79)
===========================

Functions return error as the last value. if err != nil is the standard pattern. errors.Is and errors.As unwrap wrapped errors. panic/recover handle exceptional cases sparingly.

Modules (section 79)
====================

go mod init creates a module. go get fetches dependencies. go build, go test, and go run are core commands. The go toolchain vendors reproducible builds.

Testing (section 79)
====================

Testing uses the testing package in *_test.go files. Table-driven tests are common. go test ./... runs packages. Benchmarks and examples integrate with the toolchain.

Standard Library (section 79)
=============================

net/http serves HTTP APIs. encoding/json handles JSON. database/sql connects to SQL databases. The standard library favors batteries-included production utilities.

Overview (section 95)
=====================

Go is a statically typed, compiled language designed at Google for simplicity, concurrency, and fast builds. It emphasizes explicit error handling and a small language spec.

Variables and Types (section 95)
================================

Declare variables with var or := for inference. Basic types include int, float64, string, bool, arrays, slices, maps, and structs. Zero values apply when variables are uninitialized.

Control Flow (section 95)
=========================

if, for, and switch handle control flow. Go has no while keyword; for loops cover iteration. defer schedules cleanup calls when a function returns.

Functions (section 95)
======================

Functions are declared with func name(args) returnType. Multiple return values are idiomatic, especially (value, error). Functions are first-class but not fully generic until Go 1.18+ generics.

Structs and Methods (section 95)
================================

Structs group fields. Methods attach to types via receiver functions: func (s *T) Method(). Pointer receivers allow mutation and avoid copying large values.

Interfaces (section 95)
=======================

Interfaces define behavior by method sets. A type satisfies an interface implicitly. Small interfaces such as io.Reader encourage composable designs.

Concurrency (section 95)
========================

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Error Handling (section 95)
===========================

Functions return error as the last value. if err != nil is the standard pattern. errors.Is and errors.As unwrap wrapped errors. panic/recover handle exceptional cases sparingly.

Modules (section 95)
====================

go mod init creates a module. go get fetches dependencies. go build, go test, and go run are core commands. The go toolchain vendors reproducible builds.

Structs group fields. Methods attach to types via receiver functions: func (s *T) Method(). Pointer receivers allow mutation and avoid copying large values.

Interfaces (section 110)
========================

Interfaces define behavior by method sets. A type satisfies an interface implicitly. Small interfaces such as io.Reader encourage composable designs.

Concurrency (section 110)
=========================

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Error Handling (section 110)
============================

Functions return error as the last value. if err != nil is the standard pattern. errors.Is and errors.As unwrap wrapped errors. panic/recover handle exceptional cases sparingly.

Modules (section 110)
=====================

go mod init creates a module. go get fetches dependencies. go build, go test, and go run are core commands. The go toolchain vendors reproducible builds.

Testing (section 110)
=====================

Testing uses the testing package in *_test.go files. Table-driven tests are common. go test ./... runs packages. Benchmarks and examples integrate with the toolchain.

Standard Library (section 110)
==============================

net/http serves HTTP APIs. encoding/json handles JSON. database/sql connects to SQL databases. The standard library favors batteries-included production utilities.

Go is a statically typed, compiled language designed at Google for simplicity, concurrency, and fast builds. It emphasizes explicit error handling and a small language spec.

Variables and Types (section 126)
=================================

Declare variables with var or := for inference. Basic types include int, float64, string, bool, arrays, slices, maps, and structs. Zero values apply when variables are uninitialized.

Control Flow (section 126)
==========================

if, for, and switch handle control flow. Go has no while keyword; for loops cover iteration. defer schedules cleanup calls when a function returns.

Functions (section 126)
=======================

Functions are declared with func name(args) returnType. Multiple return values are idiomatic, especially (value, error). Functions are first-class but not fully generic until Go 1.18+ generics.

Structs and Methods (section 126)
=================================

Structs group fields. Methods attach to types via receiver functions: func (s *T) Method(). Pointer receivers allow mutation and avoid copying large values.

Interfaces (section 126)
========================

Interfaces define behavior by method sets. A type satisfies an interface implicitly. Small interfaces such as io.Reader encourage composable designs.

Concurrency (section 126)
=========================

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Error Handling (section 126)
============================

Functions return error as the last value. if err != nil is the standard pattern. errors.Is and errors.As unwrap wrapped errors. panic/recover handle exceptional cases sparingly.

Modules (section 126)
=====================

go mod init creates a module. go get fetches dependencies. go build, go test, and go run are core commands. The go toolchain vendors reproducible builds.

Testing (section 126)
=====================

Testing uses the testing package in *_test.go files. Table-driven tests are common. go test ./... runs packages. Benchmarks and examples integrate with the toolchain.

Standard Library (section 126)
==============================

net/http serves HTTP APIs. encoding/json handles JSON. database/sql connects to SQL databases. The standard library favors batteries-included production utilities.

Functions return error as the last value. if err != nil is the standard pattern. errors.Is and errors.As unwrap wrapped errors. panic/recover handle exceptional cases sparingly.

Overview (section 142)
======================

Go is a statically typed, compiled language designed at Google for simplicity, concurrency, and fast builds. It emphasizes explicit error handling and a small language spec.

Variables and Types (section 142)
=================================

Declare variables with var or := for inference. Basic types include int, float64, string, bool, arrays, slices, maps, and structs. Zero values apply when variables are uninitialized.

Control Flow (section 142)
==========================

if, for, and switch handle control flow. Go has no while keyword; for loops cover iteration. defer schedules cleanup calls when a function returns.

Functions (section 142)
=======================

Functions are declared with func name(args) returnType. Multiple return values are idiomatic, especially (value, error). Functions are first-class but not fully generic until Go 1.18+ generics.

Structs and Methods (section 142)
=================================

Structs group fields. Methods attach to types via receiver functions: func (s *T) Method(). Pointer receivers allow mutation and avoid copying large values.

Interfaces (section 142)
========================

Interfaces define behavior by method sets. A type satisfies an interface implicitly. Small interfaces such as io.Reader encourage composable designs.

Concurrency (section 142)
=========================

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Functions are declared with func name(args) returnType. Multiple return values are idiomatic, especially (value, error). Functions are first-class but not fully generic until Go 1.18+ generics.

Structs and Methods (section 157)
=================================

Structs group fields. Methods attach to types via receiver functions: func (s *T) Method(). Pointer receivers allow mutation and avoid copying large values.

Interfaces (section 157)
========================

Interfaces define behavior by method sets. A type satisfies an interface implicitly. Small interfaces such as io.Reader encourage composable designs.

Concurrency (section 157)
=========================

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Error Handling (section 157)
============================

Functions return error as the last value. if err != nil is the standard pattern. errors.Is and errors.As unwrap wrapped errors. panic/recover handle exceptional cases sparingly.

Modules (section 157)
=====================

go mod init creates a module. go get fetches dependencies. go build, go test, and go run are core commands. The go toolchain vendors reproducible builds.

Testing (section 157)
=====================

Testing uses the testing package in *_test.go files. Table-driven tests are common. go test ./... runs packages. Benchmarks and examples integrate with the toolchain.

Standard Library (section 157)
==============================

net/http serves HTTP APIs. encoding/json handles JSON. database/sql connects to SQL databases. The standard library favors batteries-included production utilities.

Overview (section 158)
======================

Go is a statically typed, compiled language designed at Google for simplicity, concurrency, and fast builds. It emphasizes explicit error handling and a small language spec.

Variables and Types (section 158)
=================================

Declare variables with var or := for inference. Basic types include int, float64, string, bool, arrays, slices, maps, and structs. Zero values apply when variables are uninitialized.

==========================

net/http serves HTTP APIs. encoding/json handles JSON. database/sql connects to SQL databases. The standard library favors batteries-included production utilities.

Overview (section 173)
======================

Go is a statically typed, compiled language designed at Google for simplicity, concurrency, and fast builds. It emphasizes explicit error handling and a small language spec.

Variables and Types (section 173)
=================================

Declare variables with var or := for inference. Basic types include int, float64, string, bool, arrays, slices, maps, and structs. Zero values apply when variables are uninitialized.

Control Flow (section 173)
==========================

if, for, and switch handle control flow. Go has no while keyword; for loops cover iteration. defer schedules cleanup calls when a function returns.

Functions (section 173)
=======================

Functions are declared with func name(args) returnType. Multiple return values are idiomatic, especially (value, error). Functions are first-class but not fully generic until Go 1.18+ generics.

Structs and Methods (section 173)
=================================

Structs group fields. Methods attach to types via receiver functions: func (s *T) Method(). Pointer receivers allow mutation and avoid copying large values.

Interfaces (section 173)
========================

Interfaces define behavior by method sets. A type satisfies an interface implicitly. Small interfaces such as io.Reader encourage composable designs.

Concurrency (section 173)
=========================

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Error Handling (section 173)
============================

Functions return error as the last value. if err != nil is the standard pattern. errors.Is and errors.As unwrap wrapped errors. panic/recover handle exceptional cases sparingly.

Modules (section 173)
=====================

go mod init creates a module. go get fetches dependencies. go build, go test, and go run are core commands. The go toolchain vendors reproducible builds.

Testing (section 173)
=====================

Testing uses the testing package in *_test.go files. Table-driven tests are common. go test ./... runs packages. Benchmarks and examples integrate with the toolchain.

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Error Handling (section 188)
============================

Functions return error as the last value. if err != nil is the standard pattern. errors.Is and errors.As unwrap wrapped errors. panic/recover handle exceptional cases sparingly.

Overview (section 189)
======================

Go is a statically typed, compiled language designed at Google for simplicity, concurrency, and fast builds. It emphasizes explicit error handling and a small language spec.

Variables and Types (section 189)
=================================

Declare variables with var or := for inference. Basic types include int, float64, string, bool, arrays, slices, maps, and structs. Zero values apply when variables are uninitialized.

==========================

if, for, and switch handle control flow. Go has no while keyword; for loops cover iteration. defer schedules cleanup calls when a function returns.

Functions (section 189)
=======================

=================================

if, for, and switch handle control flow. Go has no while keyword; for loops cover iteration. defer schedules cleanup calls when a function returns.

Functions (section 204)
=======================

Functions are declared with func name(args) returnType. Multiple return values are idiomatic, especially (value, error). Functions are first-class but not fully generic until Go 1.18+ generics.

Structs and Methods (section 204)
=================================

Structs group fields. Methods attach to types via receiver functions: func (s *T) Method(). Pointer receivers allow mutation and avoid copying large values.

Interfaces (section 204)
========================

Interfaces define behavior by method sets. A type satisfies an interface implicitly. Small interfaces such as io.Reader encourage composable designs.

Concurrency (section 204)
=========================

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Error Handling (section 204)
============================

Functions return error as the last value. if err != nil is the standard pattern. errors.Is and errors.As unwrap wrapped errors. panic/recover handle exceptional cases sparingly.

Modules (section 204)
=====================

go mod init creates a module. go get fetches dependencies. go build, go test, and go run are core commands. The go toolchain vendors reproducible builds.

Testing (section 204)
=====================

Testing uses the testing package in *_test.go files. Table-driven tests are common. go test ./... runs packages. Benchmarks and examples integrate with the toolchain.

Standard Library (section 204)
==============================

net/http serves HTTP APIs. encoding/json handles JSON. database/sql connects to SQL databases. The standard library favors batteries-included production utilities.

Standard Library (section 219)
==============================

net/http serves HTTP APIs. encoding/json handles JSON. database/sql connects to SQL databases. The standard library favors batteries-included production utilities.

Overview (section 220)
======================

Go is a statically typed, compiled language designed at Google for simplicity, concurrency, and fast builds. It emphasizes explicit error handling and a small language spec.

Variables and Types (section 220)
=================================

Declare variables with var or := for inference. Basic types include int, float64, string, bool, arrays, slices, maps, and structs. Zero values apply when variables are uninitialized.

Control Flow (section 220)
==========================

if, for, and switch handle control flow. Go has no while keyword; for loops cover iteration. defer schedules cleanup calls when a function returns.

Functions (section 220)
=======================

Functions are declared with func name(args) returnType. Multiple return values are idiomatic, especially (value, error). Functions are first-class but not fully generic until Go 1.18+ generics.

Structs and Methods (section 220)
=================================

Structs group fields. Methods attach to types via receiver functions: func (s *T) Method(). Pointer receivers allow mutation and avoid copying large values.

Interfaces (section 220)
========================

Interfaces define behavior by method sets. A type satisfies an interface implicitly. Small interfaces such as io.Reader encourage composable designs.

Concurrency (section 220)
=========================

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Error Handling (section 220)
============================

Functions return error as the last value. if err != nil is the standard pattern. errors.Is and errors.As unwrap wrapped errors. panic/recover handle exceptional cases sparingly.

Modules (section 220)
=====================

go mod init creates a module. go get fetches dependencies. go build, go test, and go run are core commands. The go toolchain vendors reproducible builds.

Interfaces define behavior by method sets. A type satisfies an interface implicitly. Small interfaces such as io.Reader encourage composable designs.

Concurrency (section 235)
=========================

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Error Handling (section 235)
============================

Declare variables with var or := for inference. Basic types include int, float64, string, bool, arrays, slices, maps, and structs. Zero values apply when variables are uninitialized.

Control Flow (section 251)
==========================

if, for, and switch handle control flow. Go has no while keyword; for loops cover iteration. defer schedules cleanup calls when a function returns.

Functions (section 251)
=======================

Functions are declared with func name(args) returnType. Multiple return values are idiomatic, especially (value, error). Functions are first-class but not fully generic until Go 1.18+ generics.

Structs and Methods (section 251)
=================================

Structs group fields. Methods attach to types via receiver functions: func (s *T) Method(). Pointer receivers allow mutation and avoid copying large values.

Interfaces (section 251)
========================

Interfaces define behavior by method sets. A type satisfies an interface implicitly. Small interfaces such as io.Reader encourage composable designs.

Concurrency (section 251)
=========================

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Error Handling (section 251)
============================

Functions return error as the last value. if err != nil is the standard pattern. errors.Is and errors.As unwrap wrapped errors. panic/recover handle exceptional cases sparingly.

Modules (section 251)
=====================

go mod init creates a module. go get fetches dependencies. go build, go test, and go run are core commands. The go toolchain vendors reproducible builds.

Testing (section 251)
=====================

Testing uses the testing package in *_test.go files. Table-driven tests are common. go test ./... runs packages. Benchmarks and examples integrate with the toolchain.

Standard Library (section 251)
==============================

net/http serves HTTP APIs. encoding/json handles JSON. database/sql connects to SQL databases. The standard library favors batteries-included production utilities.

Overview (section 267)
======================

Go is a statically typed, compiled language designed at Google for simplicity, concurrency, and fast builds. It emphasizes explicit error handling and a small language spec.

Variables and Types (section 267)
=================================

Declare variables with var or := for inference. Basic types include int, float64, string, bool, arrays, slices, maps, and structs. Zero values apply when variables are uninitialized.

Control Flow (section 267)
==========================

if, for, and switch handle control flow. Go has no while keyword; for loops cover iteration. defer schedules cleanup calls when a function returns.

Functions (section 267)
=======================

Functions are declared with func name(args) returnType. Multiple return values are idiomatic, especially (value, error). Functions are first-class but not fully generic until Go 1.18+ generics.

Structs and Methods (section 267)
=================================

Structs group fields. Methods attach to types via receiver functions: func (s *T) Method(). Pointer receivers allow mutation and avoid copying large values.

Interfaces (section 267)
========================

Interfaces define behavior by method sets. A type satisfies an interface implicitly. Small interfaces such as io.Reader encourage composable designs.

Concurrency (section 267)
=========================

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Error Handling (section 267)
============================

Functions return error as the last value. if err != nil is the standard pattern. errors.Is and errors.As unwrap wrapped errors. panic/recover handle exceptional cases sparingly.

Modules (section 267)
=====================

Structs group fields. Methods attach to types via receiver functions: func (s *T) Method(). Pointer receivers allow mutation and avoid copying large values.

Interfaces (section 282)
========================

Interfaces define behavior by method sets. A type satisfies an interface implicitly. Small interfaces such as io.Reader encourage composable designs.

Concurrency (section 282)
=========================

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Error Handling (section 282)
============================

Functions return error as the last value. if err != nil is the standard pattern. errors.Is and errors.As unwrap wrapped errors. panic/recover handle exceptional cases sparingly.

Modules (section 282)
=====================

go mod init creates a module. go get fetches dependencies. go build, go test, and go run are core commands. The go toolchain vendors reproducible builds.

=====================

Testing uses the testing package in *_test.go files. Table-driven tests are common. go test ./... runs packages. Benchmarks and examples integrate with the toolchain.

Go is a statically typed, compiled language designed at Google for simplicity, concurrency, and fast builds. It emphasizes explicit error handling and a small language spec.

Variables and Types (section 298)
=================================

Declare variables with var or := for inference. Basic types include int, float64, string, bool, arrays, slices, maps, and structs. Zero values apply when variables are uninitialized.

Control Flow (section 298)
==========================

if, for, and switch handle control flow. Go has no while keyword; for loops cover iteration. defer schedules cleanup calls when a function returns.

Functions (section 298)
=======================

Functions are declared with func name(args) returnType. Multiple return values are idiomatic, especially (value, error). Functions are first-class but not fully generic until Go 1.18+ generics.

Structs and Methods (section 298)
=================================

Structs group fields. Methods attach to types via receiver functions: func (s *T) Method(). Pointer receivers allow mutation and avoid copying large values.

Interfaces (section 298)
========================

Interfaces define behavior by method sets. A type satisfies an interface implicitly. Small interfaces such as io.Reader encourage composable designs.

Concurrency (section 298)
=========================

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Error Handling (section 298)
============================

Functions return error as the last value. if err != nil is the standard pattern. errors.Is and errors.As unwrap wrapped errors. panic/recover handle exceptional cases sparingly.

Modules (section 298)
=====================

go mod init creates a module. go get fetches dependencies. go build, go test, and go run are core commands. The go toolchain vendors reproducible builds.

Testing (section 298)
=====================

Testing uses the testing package in *_test.go files. Table-driven tests are common. go test ./... runs packages. Benchmarks and examples integrate with the toolchain.

Standard Library (section 298)
==============================

net/http serves HTTP APIs. encoding/json handles JSON. database/sql connects to SQL databases. The standard library favors batteries-included production utilities.

Overview (section 314)
======================

Go is a statically typed, compiled language designed at Google for simplicity, concurrency, and fast builds. It emphasizes explicit error handling and a small language spec.

Variables and Types (section 314)
=================================

Declare variables with var or := for inference. Basic types include int, float64, string, bool, arrays, slices, maps, and structs. Zero values apply when variables are uninitialized.

Control Flow (section 314)
==========================

if, for, and switch handle control flow. Go has no while keyword; for loops cover iteration. defer schedules cleanup calls when a function returns.

Functions (section 314)
=======================

Functions are declared with func name(args) returnType. Multiple return values are idiomatic, especially (value, error). Functions are first-class but not fully generic until Go 1.18+ generics.

Structs and Methods (section 314)
=================================

Structs group fields. Methods attach to types via receiver functions: func (s *T) Method(). Pointer receivers allow mutation and avoid copying large values.

Interfaces (section 314)
========================

Interfaces define behavior by method sets. A type satisfies an interface implicitly. Small interfaces such as io.Reader encourage composable designs.

Concurrency (section 314)
=========================

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Functions are declared with func name(args) returnType. Multiple return values are idiomatic, especially (value, error). Functions are first-class but not fully generic until Go 1.18+ generics.

Structs and Methods (section 329)
=================================

Structs group fields. Methods attach to types via receiver functions: func (s *T) Method(). Pointer receivers allow mutation and avoid copying large values.

Interfaces (section 329)
========================

Interfaces define behavior by method sets. A type satisfies an interface implicitly. Small interfaces such as io.Reader encourage composable designs.

Concurrency (section 329)
=========================

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Error Handling (section 329)
============================

Functions return error as the last value. if err != nil is the standard pattern. errors.Is and errors.As unwrap wrapped errors. panic/recover handle exceptional cases sparingly.

Modules (section 329)
=====================

go mod init creates a module. go get fetches dependencies. go build, go test, and go run are core commands. The go toolchain vendors reproducible builds.

Testing (section 329)
=====================

Testing uses the testing package in *_test.go files. Table-driven tests are common. go test ./... runs packages. Benchmarks and examples integrate with the toolchain.

==============================

net/http serves HTTP APIs. encoding/json handles JSON. database/sql connects to SQL databases. The standard library favors batteries-included production utilities.

Overview (section 345)
======================

Go is a statically typed, compiled language designed at Google for simplicity, concurrency, and fast builds. It emphasizes explicit error handling and a small language spec.

Variables and Types (section 345)
=================================

Declare variables with var or := for inference. Basic types include int, float64, string, bool, arrays, slices, maps, and structs. Zero values apply when variables are uninitialized.

Control Flow (section 345)
==========================

if, for, and switch handle control flow. Go has no while keyword; for loops cover iteration. defer schedules cleanup calls when a function returns.

Functions (section 345)
=======================

Functions are declared with func name(args) returnType. Multiple return values are idiomatic, especially (value, error). Functions are first-class but not fully generic until Go 1.18+ generics.

Structs and Methods (section 345)
=================================

Structs group fields. Methods attach to types via receiver functions: func (s *T) Method(). Pointer receivers allow mutation and avoid copying large values.

Interfaces (section 345)
========================

Interfaces define behavior by method sets. A type satisfies an interface implicitly. Small interfaces such as io.Reader encourage composable designs.

Concurrency (section 345)
=========================

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Error Handling (section 345)
============================

Functions return error as the last value. if err != nil is the standard pattern. errors.Is and errors.As unwrap wrapped errors. panic/recover handle exceptional cases sparingly.

Modules (section 345)
=====================

go mod init creates a module. go get fetches dependencies. go build, go test, and go run are core commands. The go toolchain vendors reproducible builds.

Testing (section 345)
=====================

Testing uses the testing package in *_test.go files. Table-driven tests are common. go test ./... runs packages. Benchmarks and examples integrate with the toolchain.

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Error Handling (section 360)
============================

Functions return error as the last value. if err != nil is the standard pattern. errors.Is and errors.As unwrap wrapped errors. panic/recover handle exceptional cases sparingly.

Overview (section 361)
======================

Go is a statically typed, compiled language designed at Google for simplicity, concurrency, and fast builds. It emphasizes explicit error handling and a small language spec.

Variables and Types (section 361)
=================================

Declare variables with var or := for inference. Basic types include int, float64, string, bool, arrays, slices, maps, and structs. Zero values apply when variables are uninitialized.

Control Flow (section 361)
==========================

if, for, and switch handle control flow. Go has no while keyword; for loops cover iteration. defer schedules cleanup calls when a function returns.

Functions (section 361)
=======================

Functions are declared with func name(args) returnType. Multiple return values are idiomatic, especially (value, error). Functions are first-class but not fully generic until Go 1.18+ generics.

=================================

if, for, and switch handle control flow. Go has no while keyword; for loops cover iteration. defer schedules cleanup calls when a function returns.

Functions (section 376)
=======================

Functions are declared with func name(args) returnType. Multiple return values are idiomatic, especially (value, error). Functions are first-class but not fully generic until Go 1.18+ generics.

Structs and Methods (section 376)
=================================

Structs group fields. Methods attach to types via receiver functions: func (s *T) Method(). Pointer receivers allow mutation and avoid copying large values.

Interfaces (section 376)
========================

Interfaces define behavior by method sets. A type satisfies an interface implicitly. Small interfaces such as io.Reader encourage composable designs.

Concurrency (section 376)
=========================

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Error Handling (section 376)
============================

Functions return error as the last value. if err != nil is the standard pattern. errors.Is and errors.As unwrap wrapped errors. panic/recover handle exceptional cases sparingly.

Modules (section 376)
=====================

go mod init creates a module. go get fetches dependencies. go build, go test, and go run are core commands. The go toolchain vendors reproducible builds.

Testing (section 376)
=====================

Testing uses the testing package in *_test.go files. Table-driven tests are common. go test ./... runs packages. Benchmarks and examples integrate with the toolchain.

==============================

Overview (section 392)
======================

Go is a statically typed, compiled language designed at Google for simplicity, concurrency, and fast builds. It emphasizes explicit error handling and a small language spec.

Variables and Types (section 392)
=================================

Declare variables with var or := for inference. Basic types include int, float64, string, bool, arrays, slices, maps, and structs. Zero values apply when variables are uninitialized.

Control Flow (section 392)
==========================

if, for, and switch handle control flow. Go has no while keyword; for loops cover iteration. defer schedules cleanup calls when a function returns.

Functions (section 392)
=======================

Functions are declared with func name(args) returnType. Multiple return values are idiomatic, especially (value, error). Functions are first-class but not fully generic until Go 1.18+ generics.

Structs and Methods (section 392)
=================================

Structs group fields. Methods attach to types via receiver functions: func (s *T) Method(). Pointer receivers allow mutation and avoid copying large values.

Interfaces (section 392)
========================

Interfaces define behavior by method sets. A type satisfies an interface implicitly. Small interfaces such as io.Reader encourage composable designs.

Concurrency (section 392)
=========================

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Error Handling (section 392)
============================

Functions return error as the last value. if err != nil is the standard pattern. errors.Is and errors.As unwrap wrapped errors. panic/recover handle exceptional cases sparingly.

Modules (section 392)
=====================

go mod init creates a module. go get fetches dependencies. go build, go test, and go run are core commands. The go toolchain vendors reproducible builds.

=====================

Declare variables with var or := for inference. Basic types include int, float64, string, bool, arrays, slices, maps, and structs. Zero values apply when variables are uninitialized.

Control Flow (section 423)
==========================

if, for, and switch handle control flow. Go has no while keyword; for loops cover iteration. defer schedules cleanup calls when a function returns.

Functions (section 423)
=======================

Functions are declared with func name(args) returnType. Multiple return values are idiomatic, especially (value, error). Functions are first-class but not fully generic until Go 1.18+ generics.

Structs and Methods (section 423)
=================================

Structs group fields. Methods attach to types via receiver functions: func (s *T) Method(). Pointer receivers allow mutation and avoid copying large values.

Interfaces (section 423)
========================

Interfaces define behavior by method sets. A type satisfies an interface implicitly. Small interfaces such as io.Reader encourage composable designs.

Concurrency (section 423)
=========================

goroutines run lightweight concurrent tasks. channels communicate between goroutines. select multiplexes channel operations. sync and context packages coordinate shared state and cancellation.

Error Handling (section 423)
============================

Functions return error as the last value. if err != nil is the standard pattern. errors.Is and errors.As unwrap wrapped errors. panic/recover handle exceptional cases sparingly.

Modules (section 423)
=====================

go mod init creates a module. go get fetches dependencies. go build, go test, and go run are core commands. The go toolchain vendors reproducible builds.

Testing (section 423)
=====================

Testing uses the testing package in *_test.go files. Table-driven tests are common. go test ./... runs packages. Benchmarks and examples integrate with the toolchain.

Standard Library (section 423)
==============================

net/http serves HTTP APIs. encoding/json handles JSON. database/sql connects to SQL databases. The standard library favors batteries-included production utilities.

Overview (section 424)
======================

Go is a statically typed, compiled language designed at Google for simplicity, concurrency, and fast builds. It emphasizes explicit error handling and a small language spec.
